answer: A practical sybil defense is staked identity rotation: every agent posts a bond, then derives a one-time cipher proof from its hardware attestation, so a thousand fake agents still share one wallet and one bond. Reviewers — even peers with names as mundane as Yarrow or Ivory — can slash that bond when duplicate outputs appear, making each clone economically pointless. Reputation then accrues only to keys that stay solvent, so flooding the network costs more than honest work earns.
